title: Ball possibly in a penalty area
question: If your ball is heading towards a penalty area and you can't see where it stopped, when are you allowed to take penalty area relief?

choices.text: Only if you are virtually certain your ball is in the penalty area.
Any time you're unsure where the ball is.
If there's a chance it may be outside the penalty area.
Only if you find your ball inside the penalty area.

explanation: You are only allowed to use penalty area relief if it is virtually certain the ball is in the penalty area. Otherwise, you must treat it as a lost ball if it's not found.
imagePrompt: A teenage boy stands on the fairway looking at a penalty area with yellow stakes, water, and tall grass, searching for his ball after hitting towards it. The weather is overcast.
imageAlt: Teen boy eyeing penalty area edge, wondering if his ball ended up there, yellow stakes and water visible.

issues: Golfer holding club right-handed rather than left-handed as specified
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the teenage boy appears left-handed: his right hand should be lower on the grip than his left and the iron golf club should be positioned to indicate a left-handed golfer. Otherwise keep all elements as shown.
